learningObjectives: Identify the major components of the Blood–Brain Barrier.
Explain how the Blood–Brain Barrier contributes to distributed brain function.
Connect Blood–Brain Barrier physiology with clinically relevant symptoms and conditions.
Interpret structural or functional findings cautiously and in context.

anatomy.label: Endothelial cells
anatomy.detail: Continuous tight junctions limit paracellular diffusion.
anatomy.clinical: Injury increases permeability and vasogenic oedema.

anatomy.label: Tight junctions
anatomy.detail: Claudins, occludin and scaffold proteins restrict movement between cells.

anatomy.label: Pericytes
anatomy.detail: Regulate capillary stability, flow and barrier gene expression.
anatomy.clinical: Loss is linked with microvascular dysfunction.

anatomy.label: Astrocytic end-feet
anatomy.detail: Help regulate ions, water and signalling around vessels.

anatomy.label: Selective transporters
anatomy.detail: Glucose and amino acids use dedicated carrier systems.
anatomy.clinical: Transport competition and saturation affect drug delivery.
